meta_description: Prompt injection, poisoning and shadow AI expand the threat model faster than programs respond.

blocks.x: Prompt injection, poisoning and shadow AI expand the threat model faster than programs respond.

Your AI estate is an attack surface. Inventory it. is not a slogan; it is a delivery position. Across engagements the pattern repeats: programs that respect this move faster and survive audit; those that do not pay for it later — usually in the audit itself.

items: Shadow-AI discovery is the fastest risk-reduction move most enterprises can make.
Agent tool-call authorization must be separate from user identity — or agents inherit too much.
AI red-teaming with findings-to-fix tracking beats annual pen-test checkboxes.

blocks.x: Three questions to ask your current vendors

items: What is the classical baseline every proposed capability must beat, measured on identical data?
Who signs the go/no-go gate, and what evidence do they require before signing?
What did you stop last quarter, and what did the stop save us?

blocks.x: The expensive mistake is measurement retrofits: without the baseline locked in week one, every outcome claim becomes an argument instead of an audit, and the program loses its budget defense.

items: falsifiable criteria and locked baselines before build; the demo is the least important artifact.
named owners, run models and escalation paths agreed with the operating team, not for it.
replay trails, control tests and documentation as artifacts of the build — never reconstructed.

blocks.x: Injection success rates are driven below agreed thresholds only with engineered defenses.
